newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty just up vs basket, seen steady next week.
newsitem.headline: Zloty just up vs basket, seen steady next week.

text.p: The Polish zloty strenghtened a fraction against the currency basket taking advantage of thin trade, caused by difference in the value dates between domestic and European forex markets, dealers said.
They said the three-day difference between the dollar/zloty value date of December 24 and dollar/mark on December 27 furhter slowed down trade already dampened by the pre-Christmas holiday mood.
"There are only three more working days this year so nothing will happen ... unless the NBP intervenes," said Pawel Gajewski from Creditanstalt in Warsaw.

The zloty closed up at 3.31/3.19 percent from the trading band centre against yesterday's 3.23/3.18 percent. It closed at 2.8585/20 to the dollar, against 2.8570/85 on Thursday and at 1.8380/05 to the mark, against 1.8375/85.
One-day rates plunged in the morning trade and then climbed back after the central bank drained surplus money in a large two-billion zloty seven- and 14-day reverse repo operation.

The central bank cleared 2.05 billion zloty off the market, the amount of bids and cut maximum 14-day rate by 0.05 point to 21.65 percent. Simultaneously it set a maximum rate for seven days at 21.55 percent.
Overnight rates were quoted at 19.00/20.50 percent, up from opening's 18.20/18.70 percent. Tomorrow/next rates were at 21.5/21.7 percent, up from intraday lows of 18.9/19.4 percent.
Dealers said that despite tax payments deposit rates were unlikely to rise above the NBP's referential drainage rates as banks had strongly overbuilt their reserves accounts.
"There is overliquidity on the market, and it seems rates will not rise until the end of the year... unless the NBP stages one-day reverse repos," said Ewa Sokolowska from Kredyt Bank SA.
